design.summary:
Add one additive, record-only `fidelity` block to metrics.json and result.json["metrics"], built by a new module test/shiploop_e2e/fidelity.py. It reads three things the harness already has: ShipLoop's run directory (state.md accepted/history, tests/, lint/, quality/, backchain/, improve/, packets/), the normalized tool-call log (metrics.ToolLog, already one classifier for Claude, Grok and Codex), and the delivered repo's git log. It never changes a verdict, a baseline row or a run. Parts (a), (b), (e), (f) read files only and so are host-independent; (c) and (d) read the normalized calls and results. Every part is worth computing, but I trimmed each to what a scratch prototype over all 11 saved runs (20261007 and 20261008) showed to be precise.

(a) Evidence class per accepted action (script, loop, file, sentence, skipped), set against the stage table's declared check (exporter's stage_catalog and effective_exit_check read from the run's own shiploop_stage_spec.py). No sub-kinds of cited files and no test-count claim check.
(b) Full null-validation audit from the verify records.
(c) Script-owned edits through edit-tool targets and shell write targets, name-pattern kills, model commit commands, and the author histogram recorded but not attributed.
(d) Refusals with their first line, stage, and "the same first line came back", instead of "the next call succeeded".
(e) Producer packets through the exporter's own carried_markers; Improve packets through five patterns the harness owns.
(f) Engine-record fields only.
(g) Eight clauses, each with status, strength (record or heuristic) and basis, plus an explicit list of the six clauses no script checks.

Facts that shaped the design:
- callback-attempts is a keepalive counter (record register, row `callback-attempts`), so it is dropped as a refusal measure.
- shiploop_git.identity_env defers to a configured git identity and hosts._isolated_env configures one, so on Grok and Codex model and engine commits share an author (the r2 Grok log has three identities).
- Interpreter heredoc edits are not seen, because the `python3 - <<EOF` body is code and not a document.
- Three existing tests compare shiploop_failures dicts whole, so that list keeps its shape and the refusal rows live in the block.

Prototype results, which become the replay tests:
- It reproduces the 2026-10-08 null-validation audit exactly from records (34 of 34 and 30 of 30 null counts, min_tests set on 27 and 30).
- It reproduces FE-19's numbers (11 records, 33 runs, 5 distinct commands, 2 red, accepted_ran at 6 stages).
- It reproduces FE-27 (36 of 36 producer packets).
- It tells the round-1 Improve packets (no Goal and no Done when, 16 of 16) from round-2 and round-3 ones (all five, 32 of 32).
- It finds both round-1 return-plan hand edits at the run level, with 0 false positives in 11 runs.
- It finds the two incident-causing `pkill -f "node server.js"` commands.
- It finds the repeated identical refusals (r2-checkers A3, r3-grok credential screen).
It does not reproduce what needs reading: oracle strength, whether a sentence is true, rollback text, the browser case classed away.
design.for_against:
FOR:
- The round-1 to round-3 analyses spent 17 hand-mined lens reports (about 705 KB of JSON). The counting parts of them (evidence-validity, the stage-evidence tables, the packet audit counts, refusals and glue) are record reads, and the prototypes reproduce them in about 0.1 s per run.
- Every round then reports the same numbers, so a regression of an earlier fix (A2 hand commits, Improve packets restating Goal and Done when, the return-plan hand edit) shows up without anyone re-deriving it.
- The lens agents can start from a worklist (sentence-only stages, repeated refusals, edits, missing labels) instead of reading the run cold.
- It is host-neutral: file reads plus the one normalized call log.
- Nothing runs differently: it is post-run, record-only, starts no process and sends nothing to a model.

AGAINST:
- About 350 new lines plus about 40 tests, coupled to the Run Review exporter (carried_markers, load_stage_spec, stage_catalog, effective_exit_check, which another session owns) and to engine record names and packet wording.
- It cannot see the costliest defects of round 3: weak oracles (8 of 17 hand-made mutants survive), false sentences (FE-01 "15 tests pass"), the wrong rollback, the browser case classed away.
- A tidy table could be mistaken for a verdict. Mitigations: strength labels, an explicit list of unchecked clauses, record-only status.
- The `file` class is trivially gameable (cite a README), so it must never become a target.
- Heuristic absence ("no edit found") is a lower bound, never proof.

Net: worth it because the measured reproduction is exact where it applies and the cost is small, provided it stays a record and each printed line says what it did not check.

per_part.part: (a) evidence class per accepted stage
per_part.change: Implement. One row per state.md history entry, keyed by action id. Class precedence is script, then loop, then file, then sentence; 'skipped' is the engine's own 'Not applicable to this item' entry (empty evidence_refs, no headline); 'seeded' is a harness-recorded stage. Script means a record the script wrote for that action: tests/<id>-verify*.md, lint/<id>*.md, quality/<id>-terminal.json, or backchain/<id>/check-*.json. Loop means improve/<id>/receipt.md plus the improve_results entry (S-10 says this is loop mechanics only). File means at least one evidence_ref that exists and is not the stage's own run/packets, run/inbox or run/results file; the prototype confirms intake, discovery and research cite only their own packet and read as sentence (FE-08). `records` lists the kinds so a lint-only implement row reads as lint-only. `declared` comes from the run's own stage table: exporter.stage_catalog(load_stage_spec(<engine_scripts>/shiploop_stage_spec.py)) with effective_exit_check(entry, planning_review), so 'planning_review none' needs no special case. `declared_script_run_without_record` counts only outcome done (a blocked system-test has no record by design: v1230 Grok). The backchain kind shows that r1 and r2-checkers ran backchain-check and r3 did not. Reason for smaller: no per-stage tool-call counts (stage windows are 1 s wide) and no test-count claim check (see part j). Hosts: all, no events needed.

per_part.part: (b) null-validation audit
per_part.change: Implement in full; it reads only tests/*-verify*.md and is the cleanest win. Record-level counts: records, runs, distinct commands, schemas seen (anything other than shiploop-test-loop/v1 is unmeasured, not 0). Per suite (focused, regression, check): runs, counted (counts.ran is an int), ids_shown (ids non-empty and ids_missing empty), min_tests set, accepted_ran present. Then counts_null (and by suite), zero_ran, ids_missing, red (records whose run status is red, split by expect: 'red' versus 'a test ran', the probe), and the stages carrying accepted_ran (6 of 11 records in r3). For check rows: static_only, meaning every command word of a quote-aware tokenization is a reader or existence tool (grep, test, ls, cat and the like), against 'executes a program'. A naive split on | miscounted `grep "a\|b"` in the prototype, so shlex with punctuation_chars is required. Also release_verify {where, kind} from the record's `observed` key. It reproduces the 2026-10-06 audit exactly (Sonnet 34 of 34, Grok 30 of 30) and FE-19's 11/33/5/2/6. Existing script_verifications and `verifications` stay unchanged for baseline compatibility. No thresholds: counts and presence only.

per_part.part: (c) model edits of script-owned files and model commits
per_part.change: Implement three recorded facts and no author attribution. (1) Script-owned edits: a tool call whose edit-tool target (Claude Write/Edit, Grok write/search_replace, Codex file_change translated to search_replace with `paths`) or whose shell write target (`>`, `>>`, tee, cp, mv, rm, sed -i, perl -i) is in the script-owned set and not in metrics.MODEL_INPUT. The owned set is metrics.SHIPLOOP_OWNED plus the workspace-level files it misses (<ws>/return-plan.md, return-receipt.md, workspace.md) and run/timeline.json, status.md and context-index.md. Prototype over 11 runs: 2 true positives (the two round-1 runs, sed -i on return-plan.md), 0 false positives, 1 known miss (the round-1 `python3 - <<EOF ... open(p,'w')` edit, because interpreter heredoc bodies are code and a first attempt to scan them flagged 10 false positives, so it is dropped and documented). `model_glue` stays frozen so baselines compare. (2) Name-pattern kills (pkill, killall, pgrep|xargs kill, kill $(pgrep ...)): found the r2-checkers and r3-checkers `pkill -f "node server.js"` that stopped sibling Grok harnesses, with 0 false positives. The detector only reads command strings; no code or test signals a process. (3) Model commit commands are the existing glue entries with reason 'git commit/add by the model'; wrapper scripts that call ShipLoop (ToolLog.scripts, all hosts) with their run counts are recorded as detail. Authors: a `git log --format=%an` histogram of the delivered repo plus the engine workspace identity read from the run's shiploop_git.py, stored but never counted as 'model commits'. Reason: identity_env defers to a configured identity, so on Grok and Codex engine and model share an author (r2 Grok log: ShipLoop E2E 20, ShipLoop Workspace 3, the user's name 10). Making authors a signal means setting a model identity by environment variable, a behaviour change and a separate item (part l). Hosts: tool targets and shell strings on all three; known limits are a shell `apply_patch`, `git apply` and interpreter code.

per_part.part: (d) ShipLoop refusals and whether the remedy worked
per_part.change: Implement refusals from tool-result text, which is host-independent and wrapper-proof: one row per refusal with the own first line (the existing failure_line, at most 200 chars), the verb, the stage from the same stage_windows join that per_stage uses (null without a timeline), the event time, and `repeat_of` (the index of the previous refusal when the first line is identical, no other refusal sits between, and the stage is the same where known). The block's counts are refusals and repeated. The requested pairing 'next call of the same kind succeeded' is dropped: the prototype found callback verbs cannot be paired reliably because Sonnet's wrapper scripts call the CLI as python `["python3", CLI, "complete", ...]`, which SHIPLOOP_COMMAND does not match (r3-battleship: 30 done.py runs, 19 callbacks seen), and plain `next` after a refusal also prints a packet. A repeat is the positive evidence that a first fix did not clear the refusal. It is neutral about cause: the same line twice can be a misleading remedy (r3-grok credential screen at spec.md:188 twice; r1-battleship knowledge-home refusal) or an honest second failed try (r2-checkers test-author). Needs a reader, not a verdict. ToolLog.result gains an optional `t` argument and a new `refusals` list. `shiploop_failures` keeps its exact shape because 3 existing tests compare its dicts whole. Optional engine item, not here: an append-only refusal record written by the script would make this exact on every host; today it is derived from events.

per_part.part: (e) packet standalone check from disk
per_part.change: Implement. Producer packets (run/packets/<action>.md): reuse the exporter's carried_markers on the file text, loaded through the same importlib route run.review_export uses, so the harness and the Run Review page cannot disagree. Its labels purpose, operates, checked, produces, recovery are the tenet's five (Goal, how it operates, Done when/Checked by, Result template, recovery) plus where and inputs. Packets of the old layout (the exporter's IMPROVE_PACKET) are unmeasured, not missing. Improve packets (<action>-improve.md): the exporter has no table, and applying CARRIED to them gives false crosses, so the harness owns five patterns, goal (`Reviewing the returned <stage> result. Goal: `), done_when (`^Done when \(`), checked_by (`^Checked by:`), output (`^The opening file holds exactly these headings` or `^Then run: `), recovery (`^Recovery command:`). They are anchored to shiploop_navigator._goal_lines, _checked_line, _render_improve, _first_callback_lines and _run_rules, and checked against all 40 recorded Improve packets: r2 and r3 (32 of 32) carry all five, round-1 and v1230 Sonnet (16 of 16) lack goal and done_when, which is exactly the round-1 finding and its batch-3 fix. A source-pin test fails loudly if the engine's wording changes. Output: counts per label and `missing` rows {action, stage, labels}. The block stores label booleans only, never packet text. Reason for smaller: the second pattern table exists only until the exporter's owner adds Improve labels (hand-off), then it is deleted.

per_part.part: (f) honest-stop classification
per_part.change: Implement the fields the engine records, with no composite 'honest' boolean. end_state holds the engine status, stage, unaccepted_stage (the harness's pending_stage), whether status_reason is named, and for a blocked run the last accepted entry's blocked_by, awaiting {kind, no_default present} and evidence_refs existence. For a done run it holds the product-acceptance `unverified` list (entries and owners; a missing key is unmeasured, an empty list says all observed). Examples: v1230 Grok blocked access with awaiting kind present and no_default stated; r1 Grok blocked access, awaiting kind answer with options; r3 Grok stopped by request with the engine active at implement and nothing claimed. The sub-item 'the unverified requirement is named and has no recorded pass' is deferred (needs-another-run): requirement ids for a blocked run live in the worktree's spec (the delivered work dir has none), the reasons name test ids that are not in any record (TC-BROWSER), and precision is unknown. Termination (process, stop file) stays the harness's existing `termination` and is not duplicated.

per_part.part: (g) SPEC clause table
per_part.change:
Implement eight rows for the clauses a script can check, each {clause, status pass|fail|unmeasured, strength record|heuristic, basis, detail}, plus `not_script_checked`: [S-2, S-3, S-7, S-8, S-12, S-13] so a table of passes is never read as all clauses.
- S-1 (heuristic): fail if any script-owned edit, else pass.
- S-4: model_glue without the commit reason (detail lists wrapper scripts; wrappers alone do not fail, because that would invent a rule, an owner decision).
- S-5 (heuristic): fail on any model commit command.
- S-6 (record): every producer and Improve packet carries all labels, else fail with the list.
- S-9 (record): no declared script-run stage without a record, no counted run with ran 0, no passed record with a failed non-red run. Its basis text says 'oracle strength is not measured'.
- S-10 (record): every done stage whose effective exit check is 'review loop' has an improve_results entry and active_improve is null at done.
- S-11: the existing committed verdict.
- S-14: asked_user is 0 and a blocked run carries awaiting or blocked_by.
- S-15: the existing narrative block (shown versus emitted).
Status is unmeasured with a reason where the input is absent. Clauses can only fail from a found violation or a missing record, never from a threshold.

per_part.part: (h) printing and wiring
per_part.change: run._main builds the context ({engine_scripts: the_cli.parent, work, committed pass, seeded stage names}) and passes it to metrics.collect(out, run_dir, context=...). The block is also added to the explicit key tuple of result['metrics']. fidelity.lines(block) prints at most 7 'fidelity' lines after the existing 'metrics' lines (evidence classes with declared-missing; validation; edits, kills and commit commands; refusals with repeats and the first line; packets; end state; clauses with strength words and the unchecked list). A builder exception is fail-open, recorded as fidelity {error} and printed as 'fidelity skipped: <reason>', exactly like review_export. progress.py and shared_tmp_writes call collect with no context and get fidelity null.

per_part.part: (i) baseline row summary
per_part.change: Do not add to baseline_row yet. There is no history of the block to compare, and the SPEC pattern (narrative) is to score beside reliability until a style has a baseline. After three runs of one case show stable keys, add a compact {edits, model_commit_commands, kills, repeated_refusals, failed_clauses} and print a comparison only when both rows have it.

per_part.part: (j) unbacked test-count claims
per_part.change: Not now. A prototype comparing 'N tests' sentences in accepted summaries against counts.ran in earlier records flagged the true FE-01 case (r3 Battleship release-plan and release-check claiming 15 before any 15-test record) but also flagged implement results that cite the model's own earlier run (13, 30). Precision is unknown, so it is a candidate for one more round of data, not a measure.

per_part.part: (k) callback-attempts minus revision
per_part.change: Drop. The record register says callback-attempts is a keepalive counter (written by protocol._count_callback_attempt), revision also bumps on pause, halt, delegation and lint-mode, and the prototype matched the event-derived count in only 6 of 8 comparable runs.

per_part.part: (l) model identity by environment
per_part.change: Separate item, not F1. Exporting GIT_AUTHOR_* and GIT_COMMITTER_* for the host instead of a [user] config would make the engine commit as 'ShipLoop Workspace' and the model as a sentinel on every host, so authors become a real signal. It changes a run's git identity (Grok and Codex engine commits move from 'ShipLoop E2E' to the workspace identity) and so needs its own admission and a live run.

unknowns: Does the shell-edit detector hold on real Codex `zsh -lc "..."` command strings and Codex file_change events? No Codex run is on disk from 2026-10-07 and 2026-10-08. Settled by a translator-based subTest now (the quoted command is scanned whole, and file_change `paths` are read) and by regrading the first live Codex run (`--resume-run <dir> --grade-only`), which needs no host.

Precision of the edit detector: replay gives 2 true positives, 0 false positives and 1 known miss in 11 runs. The miss rate on interpreter heredocs is unknown. Settled by keeping the heuristic label, listing the commands, and re-measuring after the next 3 runs; widening to interpreter code only if a safer pattern than 'owned path near an open(..., w)' is found (the first attempt gave 10 false positives).

Whether the author histogram is worth keeping. On Claude it is informative only because this machine has no configured git identity (machine state), and on Grok and Codex it is not attributable. Settled by recording it as a fact and testing with explicit names in a temp repo; the deterministic version is part l.

How the engine workspace identity is read: a regex over the run's shiploop_git.py WORKSPACE_IDENTITY 'GIT_AUTHOR_NAME'. If the file or constant is gone, `workspace_identity` is null with a reason. A source-pin test settles drift in this repo.

Whether a lint record should make an implement stage 'script'. Decision: yes, because the stage table declares lint-gate as its complete_run and `records` shows lint-only. The record itself says it is 'not exit-criteria evidence', so the printed line names the kinds. Owner may prefer a separate 'lint' class; settled by one look at the r3 table.

Where handoff and release guards (workspace_completion_guard, the return receipt) appear: they are not in the stage table's complete_runs, so those stages read as `file` although the engine refuses without a receipt (FE-15). This is an engine fact (declare the guard in the stage table), outside this group; the block records `file` honestly.
Whether wrapper scripts that call ShipLoop should fail S-4. Left as detail only; this is an owner decision (the models write them to build the inbox result file; S-4 says the script should own that).

Wrapper-hidden verbs: a model script that calls the CLI as a python argument list is not recognised by SHIPLOOP_COMMAND. This blinds verb attribution, not refusal detection (the result text is read), and is a documented limit.
The unverified-requirement-without-a-pass check for blocked runs: deferred (see f). Settled by a design note plus one run that blocks with a spec present in the work dir.

Old packet layout (ShipLoop 1.22.0 and earlier): the producer packet is gone for reviewed stages. The block marks them unmeasured and relies on the exporter's IMPROVE_PACKET test; no compatibility shim.

The exporter's function names (carried_markers, load_stage_spec, stage_catalog, effective_exit_check, IMPROVE_PACKET) are an unwritten contract with the other session. Settled by the hand-off request to keep them and by the fail-open path plus the pin test.

Timing: stage windows are whole seconds, so a refusal near a boundary can be assigned to the neighbouring stage. `stage` is best effort and null without a timeline; `repeat_of` needs no timing when stage is null.
risks: Saved records: old metrics.json and result.json lack the key, which is absent and not an error. The exporter reads fields by name and ignores extras (checked: it reads unmeasured, stages, shiploop_failures, model_glue, planning, tool_use). A regrade of an intact run adds the block with no host. Older engine records give unmeasured parts, never zero and never a shim. shiploop_failures keeps its exact shape because 3 tests compare its dicts whole.

Other hosts: edits, kills and refusals read the normalized call log. Codex file_change reports the first path as the target, so the block reads `paths` too. A shell apply_patch or git apply is invisible. No Codex run is available to replay, so the first live Codex regrade is the proof.

Misreading: a 'pass (heuristic)' is a lower bound, and a repeated refusal is a pointer. Mitigations: strength words in the printed line, the named list of unchecked clauses, S-9's basis text saying oracle strength is not measured, README limits, and record-only status.

Gaming (Change admission): `file` is satisfied by citing any existing file, so it must not become a target. The block is never shown to the model, never changes a verdict, and an engine fix that adds records raises the script count honestly.

Coupling: the exporter (another session owns it), the engine's record file names, the stage table and the Improve packet wording. Mitigations: fail-open with a reason, a source-pin test on the engine strings, a hand-off to keep the four names, and a one-commit deletion of the harness's Improve table once the exporter owns it (S-12 within the harness).

Safety: no code and no test signals a process or starts a long-lived one. The kill detector only reads strings; the one test that exercises it patches os.kill, os.killpg and subprocess to fail if called. Real-git tests start `git` to completion only, with the machine's git config isolated (the CI git-lfs lesson). Nothing touches listeners.py or a real listener.

Cost and runtime: about 0.1 s of prototype work per run plus about 0.1 s to import the exporter, and one `git log`. The block is about 10 KB (36 stage rows) in each of metrics.json and result.json; the run report grows by at most 7 lines. progress.py is unaffected because it passes no context. A regrade of a live run is a snapshot (as today).

Personal data: the author histogram carries names. It lives only in the disposable output folder (never in baseline rows), the committed extracts anonymise names, and refusal and edit rows store the matched segment (at most 120 to 200 characters), not whole commands.

Scope creep: oracle strength and mutation survival (FE-04) are case data for cases.json and a different group; this block must not grow into them. The claim-count check is held back until its precision is known.

design.summary:
Build one opt-in probe, `--clear-at after:<stage> | inside:<stage>[:<calls>|:result]`, in a new test/shiploop_e2e/clearprobe.py. It generalizes the existing `--interrupt-at` kill-and-fresh-session block in run._main (the same `stop_when` hook in run.launch, the same `host.argv(prompt=resume_prompt(...))` with no `resume=`), so Claude, Grok and Codex all get a truly fresh context. SPEC S-6 already makes this probe the gate for moving grounding out of a packet, and every analysis so far says it was never run (round3-analysis.json: "No clear-the-context probe was run").

What it records, all computed by script from run records:
- A harness-written append-only `<out>/sessions.jsonl` (one row per host launch: kind first|fresh|continued, reason, events_line, t). The host's own events cannot give session boundaries: Grok repeats `available_commands` (r3 events.jsonl has 237, so metrics.collect reports unreported_sessions 237; r2 74).

design.for_against:
FOR:
- SPEC S-6 and the README main tenet make "a clear-the-context probe at a stage boundary and inside a stage shows no redone work" the admission test for any packet shortening, and no script computes it. The Round 1, 2 and 3 analyses and the batch-1008 design audit all list it as unrun.
- The accidental probes (r2, r3, Luna) show every measure is already computable from run records with ToolLog. The 4-in-a-row Luna first-`next` typos and the r3 slice are replayable as fixtures.
- Almost all machinery exists: the `stop_when` hook, killpg, the fresh-argv path used by `--interrupt-at`, `<out>/stop`, the SIGTERM handler, `pending_stage` and `current_stage` (inner-loop resolved), `timeline.json` accept stamps, and `ToolLog`.
- Cheap to run: hello on Sonnet.

AGAINST (and dispositions):
1. The engine-record verdict can rarely fail. S-1 makes re-acceptance impossible, and r2 and r3 both passed it. The cost record is where the information is.
   - Mitigated: fake-host modes (replacement run, rewritten accepted result, no progress) prove the verdict can fail.
   - Accepted: model-side redo is record-only. A verbatim-command comparison found 0 repeats in r3 although the model re-ran `node --test` in another shape, so a command-level verdict waits for a settled measure.
2. The resume prompt itself names the recovery command (SPEC "A resume names the CLI the run itself uses"), so the probe tests the production recovery path (prompt plus packets), not packets alone. Accepted; a bare-prompt variant would contradict that rule and is dropped.
3. Hidden channels that make the clear less clean:
   - Claude auto-memory persists per cwd slug. `~/.claude/projects/-Users-dadleet-e2e-runs-20261008-r3-checkers-sonnet-work/memory/MEMORY.md` exists, written by the model during that run.
   - `listeners.reap` kills the old session's servers, where a real /clear would not.
   - Mitigated: record `host_memory` files, set CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1 in probe sessions only (the string is present in the installed 2.1.295 binary; its effect is unverified), and document the reap difference.
4. Inside-stage placement by K tool calls is not exactly reproducible across runs. Mitigated: the `:result` form is deterministic, and the record carries `progress_on_disk`.
5. Cost and runtime: a probe is a whole run. Mitigated: no default, a cheap case and early stages, serial runs, and the stop file after the measured line.
6. Gaming: the call count could shrink because the resume prompt got richer. The prompt is under the SPEC rule and printed in the record.
7. Code size in a 2113-line run.py. Mitigated: logic lives in clearprobe.py and metrics.py, and run.py only wires it.

design.summary: Implement a smaller version of the F3 ask. Today the harness compares every run with the single last row of its (case, source, host, model, effort, planning_review) driver (run.py scan_baseline, printed as 'baseline vs ...: turns A -> B, cost $X -> $Y'), and the records show that comparison misleads in four concrete ways. (1) Build identity is wrong: the two Battleship Sonnet rows of 2026-10-06/07 (238 and 294 turns, $6.54 and $9.65) both say plugin 1.22.0 / ShipLoop 0.54.0, but their built plugin trees differ (digests c480fedcc813 vs fefadd934c4f; local_head 81e0502f vs bc1d6452) and they ran on Claude Code 2.1.291 vs 2.1.292, so a whole investigation (SonnetCostDecompositionTest, the 'cost rise decomposed' entry) explained a difference between two uncontrolled builds. Conversely HEAD over-splits: r1 Battleship (587cd90d) and r1 Checkers (5e209285) carry byte-identical plugin trees (142047ca62ed). (2) A blocked run is used as a basis: the r1 Grok run printed 'turns 503 -> 301, cost $14.17 -> $8.75' against the 2026-10-07 row, which was blocked at system-test; scan_baseline never reads verdicts or termination. (3) Rows are lost: the loop produced 7 finished-run rows and the committed baselines.jsonl at 1854938b holds 3 (r1 Checkers, r3 Battleship, r3 Checkers); r1 Battleship and r1 Grok are only in worktree b1008a, r2 Battleship and r2 Checkers only in b1009i. (4) The Grok cell is 'custom', and its prompt text embeds the run folder (--improve-skill <run>/build/...), so five runs have five different prompt.txt hashes; masking the run's own folder makes all five hash to 5ea67bf3. The design: add build, prompt, host-build, span and planning identity to the row (additive, nullable); a leaf spread.py that places a value against the earlier rows of its cell and says 'no claim possible' below 3 earlier rows, never a regression verdict; one printed 'spread' line plus a 'spread' block in result.json; skip did-not-reach-done rows as a basis; a read-only --baseline-report that unions baselines.jsonl with run folders; and a strictly sequential --repeat N. Dropped or deferred: any threshold, trimming or regression flag, overlap exclusion, a shared plugin dir across repeats, per-stage spread in the per-run print, model_calls in rows, reuse of the audit campaign.py. Size m, harness only; nothing under skills/shiploop/ or skills/shiploop-run-review/ is edited.
design.for_against: FOR. The bounded loop's rule 'halt on regression' (LEARNINGS 'Round 1') is today judged by hand against n=1 pairs; the journal itself says the Checkers +65% cost 'is inside observed run-to-run spread' while resting on Battleship rows of different builds and host builds, and the earlier entry already says to settle it 'only by repeated runs on one build (3 per host)', which is what --repeat 3 does. A replay of the proposed placement on the real sequences shows the printed line would have said 'no claim possible (n=1)' for the 294-turn Battleship row, 'no claim possible (n=1/2)' for both Checkers rises, and only from the fourth Battleship row 'within/below' with the side and the chance. The only recorded same-build pair (hello 1.19.0, tree 42797fa4f916, 194 and 254 turns, $5.37 and $7.33, 17 minutes apart, baselines rows 13-14) names no host, so the current code can never compare it: run-to-run spread of 31-36% exists on a trivial case. Planning minutes are tight (Sonnet Battleship 4.8-5.6, Checkers 5.7-7.0) while cost ranges 5.67-9.65 and 5.16-8.51, so the spread locates the variance after planning, which the owner's 30-minute planning rule can read directly. The change is script-computed from records the harness already writes (timeline.jsonl, invocation.json, prompt.txt, state.md), adds no model spend and changes no run's behaviour. AGAINST. (a) A range of n earlier rows is an upper envelope that contains build changes, so 'within' can be read as 'no regression'; mitigated by printing n, the build count, shared builds and the order-statistics fact that with no change a new run falls outside a range of n rows 2 times in n+1 (a distribution-free fact, not a threshold), and by never using the words regression, better or worse. (b) One outlier row widens the range for good; no trimming rule is added because a trim is an invented threshold; the report lists every row. (c) Every old row lacks prompt_sha256 and is not placed in any cell (the same precedent as rows without host/model/effort), so the live line starts at 'no claim possible' until a --repeat 3 supplies rows; --baseline-report --runs restores the whole history for reading now. (d) It adds about 250 lines to run.py (already 2113 lines) and about 20 tests; kept small by a leaf spread.py, by reusing baseline_row/scan_baseline/row_planning_review/metrics.timeline/planning window, and by not touching stage_diff_lines. (e) Overlap: all 3 Checkers rows and 4 of 5 Battleship rows overlapped another run (the Grok run), so excluding overlapped rows would leave nothing; the design records and reports overlap and excludes nothing.

per_part.part: P1 Row and result identity fields: plugin_sha256, prompt_sha256 (output folder masked), host_build, started/ended, planning_seconds, local_head copy
per_part.change: Reason: version strings do not identify a build (1.22.0 twice, different trees), HEAD over-splits (587cd90d vs 5e209285, same tree), prompt.txt of the Grok custom case differs per run, and Claude Code 2.1.291/292/294 was only recoverable from events. Change: run.tree_digest(plugin_dir) (sha256 over sorted relative path + file digest, skipping __pycache__ and *.pyc; 13 ms for 5.5 MB) called inside installed_versions so every path (marketplace, checkout, resumed) gets versions.plugin_sha256 at launch; run.masked_prompt_digest(prompt, out) = sha256(prompt.replace(str(out), '<output>').strip())[:12]; host_build = metrics claude_code_version for Claude, else Host.cli_version(); span from metrics.collect (min/max of the existing timeline stamps); planning_seconds = planning.window.seconds when closed. baseline_row copies them from result.json so it stays a pure function of the result dict. Verified on 9 real folders: Grok's installed copy digests equal the build dir digest after 52-104 minute runs (no host pollution).

per_part.change: Reason: the harness code changed in 66 commits in 6 days, several redefining measured quantities, and the audit harness records the same thing (campaign._settings observer_digest); but any edit changes the digest, so it can say 'may differ', never 'did differ'. Change: record sha256 over sorted test/shiploop_e2e/*.py only (not LEARNINGS.md, baselines.jsonl, cases.json) in versions.harness_sha256 and the row; informational: it is never a cell key and the report prints one line 'measured under k harness builds' only when k > 1. per_part.part: P3 spread.py leaf library
per_part.change: Reason: one place for the numbers, importable by run.py and tests, no import of run.py. MIN_EARLIER_ROWS = 3 (the owner's floor of 2026-10-09). describe(values) -> n measured, not_measured, min, median (statistics.median), max, all None-aware. place(value, described) -> claim in {within, above, below, none, not measured}, by (distance outside the range, absolute and percent), outside_chance '2/(n+1)'. text helpers for the printed line. No threshold, no word regression/better/worse; inclusive bounds.

per_part.part: P4 Cell key, matching_rows refactor and the did-not-reach-done skip
per_part.change: Reason: scan_baseline reads neither verdicts nor termination, so the blocked 2026-10-07 Grok row became the basis of r1 ('503 -> 301'). Change: factor the key into run.matching_rows(path, case, source, host, model, effort, planning_review, prompt_sha256=None) yielding (row, usable); scan_baseline and previous_row return the last usable row, so there is one implementation of the key (S-12). A row is not usable when verdicts.shiploop is False (ShipLoop did not reach done and write its report); a row with no verdicts is usable (unknown is not excluded), which keeps every synthetic test row valid. prompt_sha256, when the caller passes it (main always does), must equal the row's; a row without one is skipped, the same precedent as rows without host/model/effort. The 'nothing compared' branch of _main gains one sentence for 'earlier rows exist but none reached done'. Pass False with shiploop True (a failed check) stays usable: the cost is a complete run's.

per_part.part: P5 Printed spread line and result.json spread block
per_part.change: Reason: this is the decision aid that replaces the n=1 delta. Keep the existing 'baseline vs <last row>' line and stage_diff_lines unchanged (they locate; they gate nothing) and add one 'spread' line (two when n >= 3). Reorder _main so the scan and placement happen before result.json is written (row = baseline_row(result,...) needs only the in-memory result), then result['spread'] is set, result.json is written, review_export(out) runs, and only then the row is appended to the baseline file; wrap the file read so an unreadable baseline file yields spread {compared:false, why} and never loses result.json. A resumed, seeded, unfinished or regraded run gets compared:false with the reason (the inline condition in _main becomes run.counts_as_baseline(...) so the report uses the same predicate).

per_part.part: P6 --baseline-report with --runs union and --json
per_part.change: Reason: the committed file has 3 of the loop's 7 rows and no denominator for runs that wrote no row (Grok: 5 attempts, 1 finished done, 2 blocked, 1 resumed-then-done, 1 stopped). Change: python3 run.py --baseline-report [--baseline FILE] [--runs DIR ...] [--case NAME] [--json]; read-only, writes nothing, dispatched early like --preflight-only. run.rows_from_runs(root) reads every <root>/*/result.json and <root>/*/*/result.json, rebuilds the row with the same baseline_row, takes planning_review from the run's state.md (metrics.planning_review(metrics.engine_state(run_dir))), fills any identity field the old record lacks from prompt.txt, invocation.json plugin_dir, metrics.json and timeline.jsonl and lists them in row['recomputed']; rows are merged with the file by row['output'] (a row in both counts once). A result with resumed_run set is named 'resumed or regraded: not counted' (a regrade also sets it and the folders cannot tell the two apart: v1190 hello and r2 Grok both show resumed_run with earlier_terminations empty). Output per cell: attempts (seen, counted, pass, did not reach done, resumed/regraded, seeded, ended by the harness), builds (n, shared), host builds, harness builds, overlap counts, n/min/median/max for cost, turns, minutes, planning minutes, and the 5 stages with the widest turns range (stage totals summed by name as stage_diff_lines does). Defer: --append-missing (writes rebuilt rows into the committed file; needs the owner's OK to edit a committed data file).

per_part.part: P7 --repeat N (sequential campaign)
per_part.change: Reason: no same-build sample exists in the Sonnet cells (5 rows, 5 builds), and the journal says to settle the cost question with 3 runs on one build per host. Change: run.run_repeat(args, argv) beside run_suite, dispatched after the --suite branch when --repeat > 1; strictly one attempt at a time (a for loop over main(), no pool, no --max-parallel); output <base>/rep-<i>; each attempt gets --suite-name 'repeat:<case>-<stamp>-<hex>' so the existing row field 'suite' is the group label (no new row field); before every attempt call stale_listener_lines(None) and stop with a recorded reason if it is non-empty; stop after an attempt whose process status is timeout or stopped or after TERMINATION; a blocked or failed attempt does not stop the repeat (reliability is the thing counted). Refuse with a one-line SystemExit naming the flag: --suite, --resume-run, --grade-only, --seed-at, --interrupt-at, --continue-from, --preflight-only, --baseline-report. Writes <base>/repeat-result.json (requested N, every attempt including skipped ones as the denominator, same-build range). Each attempt builds its own plugin from the checkout: the digest reports drift if the checkout is edited mid-campaign, and the summary then says 'not a same-build sample'. Rejected: building once and passing --plugin-dir to all attempts (whether a shared plugin dir is polluted by Improve-child bindings and the run's own CLI is unverified).

per_part.part: P8 Overlap record and report
per_part.change: Reason: SPEC 'Parallel work' lists as a known limit that a row has no overlap field; the span is already in timeline.jsonl. Change: row.started/ended (epoch seconds); the report and the spread block count, per row, how many other runs' [started, ended] intersect (a.started < b.ended and b.started < a.ended) against the rows of the same data set (with --runs this includes unfinished runs), with 'unknown' for a row with no span (never 'none'). design.summary: Build three small additive records in result.json and invocation.json, none of which touches pass, the exit code or the control flow. (a) An `environment` record: host CLI version for every host, tool versions, load, display hold, sibling harnesses alive, and a headless-browser probe of a stand-in page over file: and over http loopback. The browser probe runs only where a case or `--need` declares a browser. (b) Promote the already-existing but untested `shiploop.worktree_checks` into a labelled, tri-state `product_at_stop` block. (c) A pure `outcome_class` function: PASS, FAILED, BLOCKED, STOPPED, ENVIRONMENT-SUSPECT, or null for unknown. Dropped as unevidenced or host-shaped: the free-port probe, a pmset display-state read, any mid-run probe, and reading Chrome launches out of event streams. Worktree root for every path below: /Users/dadleet/src/skill-craft/.claude/worktrees/b1010m-aaa47e. Nothing under skills/shiploop/ or skills/shiploop-run-review/ changes, and no engine or packet fact is needed. Order: SPEC amendment commit first, then red tests, then code, then the recorded-run fixture and the LEARNINGS entry.
design.for_against: FOR. All 3 non-PASS runs in 20261007 and 20261008 (v1230-battleship-grok-none and r1-battleship-grok-none blocked on Chrome, r3-battleship-grok-none stopped after a Chrome debugging session) were attributed to the environment by hand, each time with a different hypothesis (display asleep, then withdrawn; Chrome over loopback, then withdrawn). None has any environment record; no Grok or Codex result names the host CLI build; Chrome auto-updated at Oct 8 14:11:08 PDT between round 1 and rounds 2 and 3 and no record names its build. In the same 3 runs the harness reported committed false and checks 0/4 although the unreturned worktree passed 4/4 case checks. Prior decisions are respected: checks graded in the worktree stay dropped (docs/shiploop-e2e-plan-reconciliation-2026-10-04.md: it would reward a run that never delivered, S-11) and a blocked run is not given a verdict (LEARNINGS 2026-10-07). AGAINST. My own bounded probe from this shell got 1 of 6 headless-Chrome launches through while a sibling session was also launching Chrome (a machine-level probe may fail most of the time), so ENVIRONMENT-SUSPECT may be noisy; mitigation is that the class is only an overlay on runs that did not finish, the raw probe record always shows, and BLOCKED with probes passing is itself informative (it points at the host or session). The probe adds up to about 20 s before a browser-need run and about 20 s after a non-PASS one, and a Chrome hang can only be seen from outside the host, so the record cannot prove where inside the Grok host the hang is. It can only show whether the machine reproduces it.

per_part.part: (a) environment capability record
per_part.change: New test/shiploop_e2e/environment.py. Always on, about 0.1 s in total: the host CLI `--version` run with the host's own isolated env (grok, codex and claude each took 0.01 to 0.03 s and wrote no files, measured), versions of node, python3 and git, os.getloadavg and cpu count, whether the host argv is wrapped by `caffeinate -d -i` (`display_hold`, from run.keep_awake, so there is one implementation), and `other_harnesses_alive` (sibling folders of the output dir whose .harness-lock is held, via listeners.case_alive, which only reads). Only for a declared need `browser`: Chrome `--version`, the harness's own urllib GET of its stand-in over 127.0.0.1 (proxies bypassed), then `--headless=new --disable-gpu --no-first-run --user-data-dir=<throwaway> --dump-dom` on file: and on http://127.0.0.1:<ephemeral> in two parallel threads, each in its own session, ceiling 20 s, SIGKILL to that process group only, then a poll that killpg(pgid, 0) finds the group empty. The stand-in is served by an in-process ThreadingHTTPServer that is closed in `finally`. The record carries per-URL status (ok, timeout, failed, absent), seconds and title_seen. It is a record, never a gate; nothing refuses or changes a launch. A start probe runs before invocation.json is written, so it neither consumes the run deadline nor shifts the host-clock stamps; an end probe runs only for a run that did not pass, after the checks and the reap. A regrade runs no probe and restates the recorded start. DROPPED: free ports (no check failure in the 23 baseline rows or the 9 round runs traces to a port, and the case checks hold fixed 3917x and 3918x ports, so a drift-prone list would be needed), a pmset display-state read (the display explanation was withdrawn in LEARNINGS Rounds 2 and 3), any mid-run probe (it would load the machine during a run), and counting hung Chrome launches in event streams (Grok turns a hung call into a BackgroundTaskStarted update, so the reading is host-shaped). Calibrate before trusting: run `python3 test/shiploop_e2e/environment.py --need browser` ten times on a quiet machine and record the pass rate.

per_part.part: (b) product_at_stop
per_part.change: Not new: run._main already runs the case checks against shiploop['worktree'] when the run is not done and stores `shiploop['worktree_checks']` as [{command, pass}]. It misleads in four ways and has no test through run.main. A timeout reads as a product failure because returncode is dropped. The key sits under `shiploop` with no label, no engine position and no reason when nothing ran. A missing worktree and a passing run look the same (an absent key). Replace it with a top-level `product_at_stop` built by a small function `run.product_at_stop(...)`: `information_only` true, the engine status and stage, per-check pass, returncode, timed_out and a short output for non-passing checks, counts of passed, failed and timed out, or `{ran: false, reason}`. It stays absent for a run that passed. It runs in the same place (before the final listeners.reap, so a server a timed-out check leaves is reaped), with the same env (PRIOR_WORK for follow-ons) and the same 180 s per-check timeout. Remove `shiploop.worktree_checks` outright (one supported version); the only readers are run.py's printed line, iterate.learnings_message and the LearningsTest fixture, and the Run Review exporter reads none. It never touches `checks`, `committed`, `pass` or the exit code (S-11).

per_part.part: (c) outcome_class
per_part.change: Add pure `run.outcome_class(result, engine, environment_failed)` and OUTCOME_CLASSES. Order: PASS if result['pass']; BLOCKED if the engine status is blocked (detail read from state.md accepted[last history action]: blocked_by, awaiting.kind, whether awaiting.no_default is stated; no prose parsing, and an old state with no `accepted` gives by null, not a parsed guess); STOPPED if process.status is stopped or timeout, or the engine is active and termination.resume_stop is a spent budget or a spent deadline; null (unknown, with a basis line) if no host exit was observed (regrade) and the engine is not terminal; otherwise FAILED with the failing verdict names and the host's own session_stops as basis. Overlay: BLOCKED with blocked_by access or external, or STOPPED, becomes ENVIRONMENT-SUSPECT when a probe of a declared need failed at the start or the end; `ended_as` keeps the underlying class so nothing is lost. The owner's `BLOCKED-honest` becomes `BLOCKED` plus `blocked.structured` (the engine accepted a blocked result naming who can unblock it and, for a person, an awaiting with no_default). Honesty itself is a judgement and S-9 forbids scoring it by script. `unverified` (count and items) is copied from the engine's own accepted records as an optional extra; drop it first if the batch grows. `pass`, the exit code, STOPPED headers and the S-14 behaviour (a blocked run is never resumed or answered) are unchanged. Also: a `## Ended as` section in mismatch.md pre-answers triage question 2; baseline_row gains outcome_class and host_cli_version.

design.summary: Add one optional, record-only `quality` block to result.json, computed by script from the delivered repo after the case checks, and fix the three hygiene gaps. The block holds a held-out acceptance set (a), a mutation ratio of the delivered tests on a copy (b) and a headless-browser observation (c). The hygiene fixes are the Claude auto-memory write (d), check text in the harness argv (e) and port contention (f). I measured the proposed measures on 8 saved deliveries before proposing them. Mutation detected ratio spans 0.56 to 0.91 and singles out r3 Battleship, which is the run the hand analysis found weak. The Checkers acceptance set reproduces the hand-found off-board defect in r3 only, and r1 and r2 pass it. The Battleship acceptance set passes 5 of 5 deliveries, so it shows a ceiling effect. I trimmed four things. I dropped case-declared mutants because delivered file names are the model's choice (game.js, lib/game.js, rules.js). I dropped page mutation and browser interaction (needs CDP), Checkers kings (needs a reference engine), and a general harness-vs-harness concurrency refusal. Nothing under skills/shiploop/ or skills/shiploop-run-review/ is touched. One lead for the engine side (headless Chrome often does not exit after writing its output) is flagged separately. Phasing is SPEC commit first (own commit, 2026-10-09), then ports and lease (f), argv scrub (e), host profile (d), quality module with check scripts and case data (b, a, c), and last the journal entry with a compact evidence extract.
design.for_against: For: the harness grades pass/fail and cost, while every fidelity or quality judgement was a hand-mined multi-agent pass. The pending stage-vs-none decision has no outcome measure, and S-9's known limit (oracle strength is model-judged; 3 page mutants passed all 15 Battleship tests) is unmeasured by script. All measures read only the delivered repo, so they are host-independent and add no model cost. Measured runtime was 25-152 s of mutation per run (sequential, 33-108 mutants) and about 1 s for the UI observation, against 13-80 minute runs. Each part is additive and optional, and a failing facet never changes `pass`. Against: n is 1 per cell and the products differ per run, so a mutation ratio compares tests-to-implementation, not like with like. Equivalent mutants cap the ratio below 1 and flip a few mutants between killed and timeout under load (the totals stayed identical across two sweeps). Held-out checks are my reading of the prompt (recorded in each check's `source`). Battleship's black-box set cannot discriminate today. No stage-vs-none decision is possible from these measures yet, because Sonnet has only been run with `stage` and Grok only with `none`, so host and mode are confounded; the harness refuses cross-mode comparison by design. Adversarial dispositions: gaming is mitigated (nothing is a verdict or threshold, held-out names stay out of argv and are grep-checked in host events); wrong-repo mutation is mitigated (a copy, hash-checked in a test); process leaks are mitigated (own session, group kill, `listeners.reap(out)` after the phase); a refused launch while :3000 is bound is accepted (it follows the existing stale-listener precedent and the contamination evidence).

per_part.part: (a) held-out acceptance set per case
per_part.change: Add `acceptance` (list of {id, kind: stated|robustness, command, source, needs_ports?}) plus `acceptance_source` to the battleship and checkers cases; battleship-scoring inherits through `follows`, as `checks` do in `load_case`. Commands are `python3 "$E2E_CHECKS/<case>_accept.py" <id>` scripts in checks/, in the style of csv_report.py and seat_service.py. They are black box over HTTP on an ephemeral port, started from the exported copy (`PORT=<free> node server.js`). Run after `run_checks` in `_main`. Record-only: they never touch `pass`. The `kind` split stops harness-author robustness expectations (unknown game id, malformed JSON, out-of-range coordinates) from reading as prompt requirements. Checkers v1 covers red-first, illegal move keeps the turn and the {ok, turn, winner} shape (off-board and negative targets), turn alternation, mandatory jump for both colours, and removal of the jumped piece (a black recapture onto the captured square is accepted). Kings are deferred: they need a recorded line or reference engine that two more passing deliveries can calibrate. Battleship is a thin regression net: exact title, distinct ids, sweep ending in gameOver on the final sinking shot, game independence, and the robustness set. Calibrate every script against a hermetic reference server with a defect switch before it is admitted (my first sweep draft failed 4 of 5 good deliveries because it kept firing after gameOver). per_part.part: (b) mutation score of the delivered tests
per_part.change: New test/shiploop_e2e/quality.py. Export the delivered files (`git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard` of work/, no .git) to <out>/quality/copy; never touch work/. Generic text operators from one catalog keyed by extension (JS only now; others report 'no operator catalog for .py', not zero): eq-flip (===, !==), rel-bound (< <=, > >=), logic-flip (&& ||), bool-flip, arith-flip (spaced + -), and bound-literal (the literal after a relational operator, +1). Comments and string/template bodies are masked. Targets are `.js/.mjs/.cjs` outside test, tests, __tests__, node_modules, docs and system. Baseline gate: the case's `quality.mutation.command` (node --test) must exit 0 and count at least 1 test on the clean copy, else `{observed:false, reason}` (a red baseline would 'kill' every mutant; the three baselines I saw red were my own leaked port-3000 listener). Each mutant runs sequentially (delivered tests bind :3000 and a fixed port in parallel would collide), in its own session with output to files, timeout max(10 s, 20x baseline), group kill, original text restored in a finally. A timeout counts as detected but is recorded separately; a syntax-error marker makes it `invalid` and drops it from the ratio. Cap at 120 mutants by deterministic stride (`sampled` recorded), phase ceiling 600 s with remaining mutants recorded `not_run` and `complete:false`. Report `detected_ratio`, by_file and up to 40 survivors (file, line, op, from, to) as the human diagnostic. No threshold. DROP case-declared mutants (file names are not stable across deliveries) and page/HTML mutation (the gap is reported by (c) and the model's own browser check).

per_part.part: (c) UI observation where a browser is available
per_part.change: `quality.observe_ui(copy, spec, out, browser)` with case data `quality.ui = {start, path, title}`. Start the product on an ephemeral PORT as an own-session child, fetch the static HTML with urllib, then run `<browser> --headless=new --disable-gpu --no-first-run --no-default-browser-check --user-data-dir=<tmp> --screenshot=<out>/quality/ui.png --dump-dom <url>` with stdout to a FILE (not a pipe). Poll for '</html>' in the dump plus a non-empty PNG, then kill the browser's process group; do NOT wait for the browser to exit, because on this machine Chrome 154.0.8037.99 wrote both at 0.4-0.6 s and then usually did not exit. The browser comes from the environment group's capability probe when it exists, otherwise a local `find_browser()` (macOS app path, then shutil.which for google-chrome, chromium, chrome); none found is `{observed:false, reason}`. No click or console-error observation yet: that needs CDP over a websocket, so it is needs-another-run. This does not close the 'page mutants pass' gap for runs without a model-written browser check; it records that the page loads and builds its DOM.

per_part.part: (d) isolation hygiene: Claude auto-memory

Behaviour change: the model loses the memory prompt, so the first Claude rows after the change are a new baseline; record it, do not gate on it.

per_part.part: (e) check strings out of argv
per_part.change: Add `--prompt-file` and `--check-file` (a JSON list) to `parser()`, read in `load_case`, and a `scrub_argv()` called only under `if __name__ == '__main__'`: when `--prompt`, `--check` or their `=` forms are on sys.argv, write them to 0600 temp files and `os.execv` the same interpreter with the file flags. The pid is unchanged, a SIGHUP ignored by nohup stays ignored, handlers are installed after the exec, and the temp files are unlinked at exit. `main(argv)` is untouched, so the existing tests that pass `--check` in-process still work. Reason: a convention would not have stopped it. The r3 Checkers model's `pkill -f 'node server.js'` matched the Grok harness because that harness's argv carried every --check string, and the model then printed that argv with pgrep (events 550 and 570). The same argv would also expose held-out names to a model. Remaining known exposure: Claude (`-p <prompt>`) and Codex (last argv element) carry the case prompt in the host's argv because stdin must stay closed (S-14); the prompt has 'server.js' but not 'node server.js'; mitigated by (f) and the engine-side R3-3 sentence. Related finding to hand to the owner: Grok `none` runs are launched with --prompt/--check, so their baseline rows sit under case 'custom' with style null and compare with any other custom run (rows 2026-10-06T18:17 and 2026-10-07T10:17); a first-class `--planning-review` option on a named case would key them correctly. per_part.part: (f) refuse on busy declared ports; serialize sharing cases
per_part.change: Declare `ports` (with `ports_source`) per case: battleship [3000, 39171, 39172, 39173]; battleship-scoring adds [39174, 39175, 39176]; checkers [3000, 39181, 39182, 39183]. 3000 is there because both prompts state it as the default, and the models' default-port checks and delivered tests bind it. In listeners.py add a per-port flock lease under /tmp/shiploop-e2e-leases-<uid> (kernel-dropped on any death, same idea as `hold_case`) with `hold_ports` and `port_holders`. In run.py add `refuse_busy_ports(ports)` beside `refuse_stale_listeners`, before the output folder exists. It refuses a launch (and --preflight-only) when `listeners.observe()` shows a listener on a declared port (not a bind probe: on macOS 127.0.0.1:3000 and *:3000 coexisted, so a bind test gives a false 'free') or another live harness holds the lease; the message names pid and case folder, with no override, like the stale-listener rule. Take the lease for the whole run after the case lock; a --grade-only regrade takes none, and only acceptance entries marked `needs_ports` run if a non-blocking lease succeeds, else `not_run: port 3000 busy`. `run_suite` merges chains whose effective port sets intersect into one sequential group (`suite_groups`), so the 'batch' suite keeps seat-reservations concurrent with the battleship chain while battleship and checkers serialize. Honest scope: the check ports of Battleship and Checkers are disjoint, so a check-port lease alone would not have prevented the Grok/Checkers incident; what ties them is :3000 (stated in both prompts) and the process-name pattern, which (e) removes from the harness argv.
